source_quotes.quote: #6 [emmy, finding] [current; not cited by the joint ledger] Executed emmy/response_audit.py (standard-library Python; exact artificial three-level Hamiltonian, NOT methanol, VQA, or hydration). A weak transition of weight 0.005 at 0.1 eV alongside weight 1 at 4.5 eV can be omitted with normalised TCF error everywhere below 0.004976, yet the static susceptibility is underestimated by 18.37%. Moving that weak transition to 3 eV reduces the same omission error to 0.744%. The exact spectral sum agrees with independent small-field ground-energy curvature, and analytic damped finite-time integration agrees with Simpson quadrature. Thus P’s reported small normalised TCF errors do not alone certify Q-relevant static response; a gap/omitted-weight bound is needed. This is a conditional error example, not evidence of low-energy channels in Q’s neutral organic fragments. Results and source hashes: emmy/response_audit_results.json. P-primary.pdf and raw/text hashes match pinned metadata; Q raw and supplied text hashes are identical.

#6 [emmy, idea] [corrected by #19; not cited by the joint ledger] Precise transfer construction (derived, not in either source): for fixed nuclei and frozen MM charges define \(H(s)=H_0+sV\), where \(V\) is the complete solvent electrostatic potential operator, including its nuclear scalar. If the electronic ground state is nondegenerate and differentiable along the path, \(E_{\rm ind}=E(1)-E(0)-E\prime(0)=\int_0^1(1-s)E\prime\prime(s)\,ds\). Define the connected correlator \(C_s(t)=\langle\delta V\exp[-i(H(s)-E(s))t/\hbar]\delta V\rangle_s\). Then \(E\prime\prime(s)=(2/\hbar)\lim_{\eta\to0^+}\int_0^\infty e^{-\eta t}\operatorname{Im}C_s(t)\,dt=-2\sum_{n>0}|V_{0n}(s)|^2/\Delta_n(s)\). P Section 3 measures general Hermitian-operator overlaps, so this is an admissible adaptation after replacing its exciton Hamiltonian and state preparation. It targets nonuniform-field induction without reconstructing the full density-response kernel. One vacuum correlator supplies only the quadratic term; nonlinear response needs multiple coupling values and new ground states. It remains a potentially expensive consistency check, not a speed-up or hydration observable. Ada can assess identifiability while I verify this identity and finite-time bias on a reproducible two-level control.

#17 [emmy, finding] [current; not cited by the joint ledger] Added emmy/response-derivation.json with the response-to-induction derivation, assumptions, error bounds, resource account and exact source metadata/exposure. For a positive electronic gap bound \(d_s\), variance \(W_s=\operatorname{Var}_s(V)\), regulator \(\eta\), propagation time \(T\), and uniform absolute correlator error \(e_s\), curvature-error bounds are respectively \(2W_s(\hbar\eta)^2/d_s^3\) for regulator bias, \(2W_s e^{-\eta T}/d_s\) for the tail, and \(2e_s(1-e^{-\eta T})/(\hbar\eta)\) for correlation error. Integrate with weight \((1-s)\) and add coupling quadrature error. Nine exact-model checks of the first two bounds pass in the updated response-check.json; molecular gap/variance premises remain unverified. This gives an energy-unit acceptance criterion, unlike optical plot agreement. Existing response-function prior work also flags weak-pole measurement cost: [Kosugi and Matsushita, publisher abstract](https://journals.aps.org/prresearch/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevResearch.2.033043). No new general response algorithm is claimed.

#19 [emmy, correction] [current; not cited by the joint ledger] Qualification to #6 and #11: the spectral sum and curvature identity use a consistently defined interacting electronic Hamiltonian. Substituting a bare Kohn-Sham orbital Hamiltonian would not reproduce self-consistent B3LYP response; orbital/density response and the exchange-correlation kernel matter. The exact-diagonalisation comparator must share the same electronic active space and perturbation as the quantum estimator, while comparison to B3LYP/cc-pVTZ or higher-level molecular response requires separate basis, active-space and orbital-relaxation convergence. Ground-state energy agreement or a symmetry reduction valid only for the unperturbed Hamiltonian does not certify retention of all perturbation-coupled response states. This does not alter the exact-model algebra or results in #15-17.

#24 [emmy, finding] [current; adopted by the joint ledger #4] Final sharpening of #14, consistent with Ada #20: an EMLE versus reference induction discrepancy must be separated into nonlinear response and representation/fitting error within linear response. At the same frozen geometry, solvent potential, basis and electronic reference, define \(E_{\rm quad}^{\rm ref}=-\chi_{WW,0}^{\rm ref}(0)/2\), \(\delta_{\rm nl}=E_{\rm ind}^{\rm ref}-E_{\rm quad}^{\rm ref}\), and \(\delta_{\rm repr}=E_{\rm quad}^{\rm ref}-E_{\rm ind}^{\rm EMLE}\). Then exactly \(E_{\rm ind}^{\rm ref}-E_{\rm ind}^{\rm EMLE}=\delta_{\rm nl}+\delta_{\rm repr}\). This is an algebraic diagnostic, not a new response theorem or observed molecular result. Use unscaled EMLE for this first comparison, with static energies removed consistently. Q manuscript pp.13-17 supplies the geometry-dependent Thole construction and QM/MM decomposition; pp.20-21 reports comparatively small induction-fitting improvements. P pp.7180-7182 supplies a possible correlation estimator, but its optical exciton Hamiltonian does not supply the electronic reference required here. The exact spectral formula in #10 assumes eigenstates of the explicitly specified electronic Hamiltonian; an approximate reference must instead use curvature/response consistent with its own energy calculation, not substitute P optical transitions. Compute the nonlinear residual first from finite-field energies and vacuum curvature, then use integrated response only as an independent closure or estimator check. A small nonlinear residual would redirect attention to representation, static interactions, or solvent/LJ compatibility without establishing which explains the hydration bias. A large residual still needs electronic-reference convergence and ensemble free-energy impact. This decomposition strengthens the classical-first decision and preserves correlated-response and estimator-benchmark alternatives. Established evidence remains synthetic closure, estimator-invariance/time-window checks, and source-specific limitations. Unresolved: validated molecular configurations and EMLE outputs, residual magnitude/sign, experimental hydration benefit, causal LJ attribution, benchmark novelty and full quantum resource cost. No scientific verdict is awarded.
